questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A clinician notes satisfaction from each extra unit of a good falls as consumption rises; what is this called?
questions.explanation: Falling satisfaction from extra units is diminishing marginal utility. The distractors reverse or deny the trend or confuse totals.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: When marginal utility is positive, what happens to total utility?
questions.explanation: Positive marginal utility adds to total utility, so total rises. The distractors reverse or confuse the relationship.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A consumer maximizes utility by allocating spending so that what is equal across goods?
questions.explanation: Utility maximization requires equal marginal utility per dollar across goods. The distractors ignore prices or use totals.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: In a single-good setting, the consumer stops buying when marginal utility equals what?
questions.explanation: The consumer buys until marginal utility equals price. Income, total utility and average utility do not set the stopping point.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Marginal utilities of three units are 10, 8, and 5; what is total utility of three units?
questions.explanation: Total utility is the sum of marginal utilities: 10 plus 8 plus 5 equals 23. The value adds the marginal contributions.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Why does marginal utility typically diminish as consumption increases?
questions.explanation: As wants are satisfied, extra units add less satisfaction. Price, income and supply do not explain the decline.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Consumer surplus from a demand schedule
questions.stem: Willingness to pay for units is 10, 8, 6 and price is 6; what is consumer surplus?
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus is (10-6)+(8-6)+(6-6)=4+2+0=6. The value sums the gaps above price.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal benefit and the demand curve
questions.stem: The demand curve reflects what concept?
questions.explanation: Demand reflects marginal benefit. Cost, fixed cost and average utility are not the basis.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: At satiation, marginal utility becomes what?

options.misconception: confuses beyond satiation with at satiation

questions.explanation: At satiation, marginal utility is zero. Positive MU occurs before satiation and negative beyond it.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A budget line shows what?
questions.explanation: The budget line shows affordable combinations given income and prices. Optimum, equilibrium and production possibilities are different.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Income is 60 dollars and price of good X is 5 dollars; what is the X-intercept of the budget line?
questions.explanation: The X-intercept is income divided by price of X, which is 60 divided by 5 equals 12. The value is maximum X affordable.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Budget line response to a price change
questions.stem: If the price of good X falls, the budget line does what?
questions.explanation: A lower X price rotates the budget line outward on the X-axis. Income changes cause parallel shifts.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A price change alters both real income and relative prices; which effect is the substitution effect?

options.text: The response to changed real income
The response to changed relative prices

questions.explanation: The substitution effect is the response to changed relative prices. The income effect is the response to changed real income.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.stem: Using the table, what is the change in quantity demanded when price rises?
questions.explanation: Quantity falls from 6 to 4, a decrease of 2. The distractors reverse, deny or mismeasure the change.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS

questions.stem: When the price of good X rises, the substitution effect leads consumers to do what?

options.text: Buy less X and more of substitutes

questions.explanation: Higher X price makes substitutes relatively cheaper, so consumers buy less X. The distractors reverse or deny the effect.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Total effect of a price change
questions.stem: The total effect of a price change equals what?
questions.explanation: Total effect is the sum of income and substitution effects. The distractors subtract or omit one effect.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

The income effect outweighs the substitution effect

questions.explanation: Giffen goods require the income effect to dominate the substitution effect. The distractors reverse or deny the condition.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: For a normal good, a price increase leads the income effect to do what?
questions.explanation: For a normal good, lower real income reduces quantity demanded. The distractors reverse or deny the effect.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: If a consumer chooses bundle A when bundle B is affordable, what is revealed?

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: If bundle A was chosen over B at original prices, and A is still affordable at new prices, what does revealed preference imply?

options.text: A is still at least as preferred as B

questions.explanation: If A was chosen and remains affordable, A is at least as preferred. The distractors reverse or misstate the implication.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: The weak axiom of revealed preference
questions.stem: The weak axiom of revealed preference says what?

options.text: Consumers always choose the cheapest bundle
A and B must always cost the same
If A is chosen over B, B cannot be chosen over A when A is affordable

questions.explanation: The weak axiom forbids choosing B over A when A is affordable after A was chosen over B. The distractors misstate the axiom.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Spotting a weak axiom violation in data

stimulus.body: At prices (2,2), choose (4,1); at prices (1,3), choose (1,4). Both bundles affordable in both cases.

questions.stem: Using the table, is there a WARP violation?

options.text: Yes, because both bundles were chosen when the other was affordable

questions.explanation: Each bundle was chosen while the other was affordable, violating WARP. Quantity or price differences do not excuse it.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.stem: Observed choices can reveal a consumer's income only if what is known?

questions.stem: Supply price rises linearly from 2 to 6 as quantity rises from 0 to 4; market price is 6; what is producer surplus?
